You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Validated on task-f6b8e3af. A full separator row or column splits two panels. Align the panels cell-for-cell; emit a grid the size of the first panel, with color 2 wherever both corresponding cells are nonzero and 0 otherwise. Ignore any extra rows/columns in the second panel if dimensions differ (demo had 7x6 vs 8x6 and output was 7x6). The panels may use different nonzero colors (demo 1 vs 4) or the same color (test 7 vs 7); only overlap matters. Separator is omitted. This recurrent instance was solved on task-f6b8e3af: 22x4 panels separated by a full 5 column; right-panel nonzeros at (row 1,col 0), (12,3), and (18,2) overlapped nonzero left cells, yielding a 22x4 output of 2 at those positions and 0 elsewhere.

Additional confirmed horizontal-split test for task-f6b8e3af: a 27x10 grid had a full separator row 13 (color 3), with 13x10 panels above and below. Upper panel used 0/9; lower panel used 0/7. Output was 13x10, with 2 at positions where both aligned cells were nonzero and 0 otherwise (separator omitted). The lower panel's zero positions, using zero-based local coordinates, were (2,5), (4,8), (4,9), (6,1), (6,4), (6,6), (6,8), (8,0), (8,4), (8,7), (8,8), (10,8), (10,9), (11,1), and (12,9). The accepted 13x10 result was computed as the pixelwise nonzero intersection.

Further confirmed horizontal test for task-f6b8e3af: 27x8 input, full separator row 13 (color 9), two 13x8 panels. Upper panel used 0/1, lower 0/3. The accepted output was 13x8, color 2 exactly where both aligned cells were nonzero and 0 otherwise. Upper-panel zero coordinates (row,column; zero-based): (0,0), (1,0), (1,2), (2,5), (3,6), (4,5), (5,1), (5,6), (6,4), (8,1), (8,7), (9,1), (9,5), (10,1), (12,7). Lower-panel zero coordinates: (0,3), (0,4), (1,3), (1,7), (2,2), (3,0), (3,4), (4,7), (5,3), (5,6), (6,1), (7,6), (8,7), (9,0), (9,4), (10,1), (10,2), (12,3), (12,7). Submitted overlap grid was accepted. This independently confirms horizontal split, separator omission, 0-based identical-coordinate alignment, and 2/0 output for these colors and dimensions.

Another accepted horizontal-split test for task-f6b8e3af: 29x18 input with full separator row 14 (color 8), splitting into two 14x18 panels. Upper panel used 0/5 and lower used 0/4. Correct output was 14x18, with color 2 exactly where both aligned cells were nonzero, and 0 elsewhere; separator omitted. This case confirms the rule for 18 columns and distinct sparse colors.
